items.q: Match the macro-priority to the page's comorbidity marker — 1) Heart 2) Kidney 3) Glycemic/weight line 4) Better-outcome addition … A) HF/ASCVD B) Albuminuria C) HbA1c and weight to metformin D) SGLT-2 inhibitor ± GLP-1 analogue
items.exp: The treatment flow marks HbA1c/weight leading to metformin, heart HF/ASCVD and kidney albuminuria as macro priorities, and SGLT-2 inhibitor ± GLP-1 analogue for better outcome; the lower flow also labels a reserved drug as DPP-4 inhibitors and Gliclazide. (Book p935)

items.q: Assess the SGLT-2 counselling list: I Euglycemic ketoacidosis is listed. II Mycotic and genital infection are listed.
items.exp: The SGLT-2 side-effect advice lists euglycemic ketoacidosis, mycotic infection and genital infection. (Book p935)

items.q: Which blood-pressure targets are written under comorbidity-driven treatment?
opts: Below 130/80 without kidney disease and below 120/80 with kidney disease
Below 120/80 without kidney disease and below 130/80 with kidney disease
items.exp: The page gives <130/80 without kidney disease and <120/80 with kidney disease. (Book p935)

items.q: What LDL target is written for a diabetic patient over 40 years with cardiovascular, peripheral vascular or heart disease?
items.exp: The LDL target branch for CVD/PVD/heart disease is <55 mg/dL. (Book p935)

items.q: Match the LDL-risk branch to the printed target — 1) Normally 2) Diabetic over 40 without risk factors 3) Diabetic over 40 with one risk factor 4) CVD/PVD/heart disease … A) <130 mg/dL B) <100 mg/dL C) <70 mg/dL D) <55 mg/dL
items.exp: The LDL flowchart gives normally <130, no risk factors <100, one risk factor <70, and CVD/PVD/heart disease <55 mg/dL. (Book p935)

items.q: Which statin doses are written below the LDL target flowchart?
items.exp: The treatment line states rosuvastatin 20 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg. (Book p935)

items.q: What aspirin dose is written for a diabetic patient over 40 years with one risk factor?
items.exp: The aspirin line says add 75 mg aspirin for the listed over-40 diabetic patient with one risk factor. (Book p935)

items.q: A patient with the page's NASH label is being managed. Which investigation and treatment pair is written?
opts: Fibroscan recommended; semaglutide and saroglitazar listed
ECG recommended; metformin and insulin listed
ERCP recommended; tacrolimus and aspirin listed
Bone scan recommended; gliclazide and degludec listed
items.exp: The NASH line recommends Fibroscan and lists semaglutide and saroglitazar. (Book p935)

items.q: Saroglitazar is labelled a dual PPAR-___ + γ agonist.
items.exp: The NASH treatment line calls saroglitazar a dual PPAR-α + γ agonist. (Book p935)

items.q: Assess the proteinuria rule: I ACE inhibitor, SGLT-2 inhibitor and finerenone are listed. II Finerenone is labelled a nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist.
items.exp: The proteinuria line lists ACE inhibitor, SGLT-2 inhibitor and finerenone, identifying finerenone as a nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist. (Book p935)

items.q: Match the over-40 diabetic risk factor to the exact examples — 1) First 2) Second 3) Third 4) Fourth … A) Hypertension B) Dyslipidemia C) Swelling D) Family history of CKD
items.exp: The risk-factor line lists hypertension, dyslipidemia, swelling and family history of CKD before the 75-mg aspirin instruction. (Book p935)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the treatments named for proteinuria?
items.exp: ACE inhibitor, SGLT-2 inhibitor and finerenone are listed for proteinuria; semaglutide appears in the NASH line. (Book p935)
